advisory.finding: `_normalize_transition_force` emits the `force=True is deprecated` DeprecationWarning whenever `force` is a bool, including `force=False` — a legacy caller who explicitly passes `force=False` (i.e. NOT forcing) receives a warning telling them to use `force="<reason>"`, which is misleading and spurious for a non-forcing call.

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py:78 `rebar.transition(parent, "open", "closed", force=True, repo_root=str(rebar_repo))` — a live consumer using `force=True` on a close (asserts only the children invariant, so it does not exercise the verifier-bypass change)
advisory.finding: The deprecated boolean `force=True` alias on `rebar.transition(..., target_status='closed')` now silently bypasses the completion-verification close gate, whereas before unification a boolean `force` armed only the start-work gate and the close-gate bypass required the separate `force_close` param. Existing library callers passing `force=True` on a close under `require_completion_verification_for_close` will now skip the verifier and close-without-signature where they previously ran the verifier.
scenarios: A library caller that historically wrote `rebar.transition(tid, 'in_progress', 'closed', force=True)` intending only a gate-agnostic force now bypasses the completion verifier and closes without a signature under a repo with the completion gate enabled.
